prompt: A company models profit in thousands of dollars over months by $P(m) = -(m - 2)(m - 11)$. Profit is exactly zero in two months. What is the LATER of those two months?
hint: Zero profit means $P(m) = 0$, so one of the factors must be zero.

hints.text: Zero profit means $P(m) = 0$, so one of the factors must be zero.
Solve $m - 2 = 0$ and $m - 11 = 0$ to find the two zero-profit months, then choose the later one.
The two months are $2$ and $11$, so the later zero-profit month is month $11$.

explanation: Profit is zero when the product is zero, so set each factor equal to zero.
Solving $m - 2 = 0$ gives month $2$, and solving $m - 11 = 0$ gives month $11$.
Month $11$ comes after month $2$, so the later zero-profit month is $11$.

alternativeExplanations.title: Sketch the profit story
steps: Because of the minus sign out front, the curve is an upside-down U.
It starts at zero in month 2, rises to a peak, then falls.
It hits zero again in month 11 — that is when the good stretch ends.
